symptomShortText: Assembly fitters cut their hands on hub bores

defect.defectText: Raised metal ridge at bore mouth

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-3301, Shift A - ran the standard cycle, no deviation logged
EQ-BROACH01-002, broach tool ran 41,200 strokes against a 30,000 stroke replacement limit; cutting edges rounded and pushed material instead of shearing it
DOC-7740 Rev C - broaching instruction current, cycle parameters unchanged
Forging cert PASS, hardness 198 HB within band

fiveWhyChain.question: Why is there a raised metal ridge at the bore mouth?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Ridge measured 0.28mm against a 0.05mm maximum - the broach pushed material up instead of shearing it off

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did the broach push material instead of shearing it?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Its cutting edges were rounded from wear after 41,200 strokes against a 30,000 stroke replacement limit

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was a worn broach still in the machine? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: Broach life is tracked on a paper tally at the machine and nobody owns it, so the replacement point passed unnoticed

actions.actionText: Quarantine batch B-49688 and inspect the bore mouth of all H22 hubs in WIP and finished stock
Replace the worn broach on EQ-BROACH01-002 and deburr the 74 affected hubs
Move broach stroke counting into the PM system with an automatic work order at 90% of tool life, so replacement no longer depends on a paper tally

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Stroke count from the PM log pinned the start date within one shift
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Tool life was tracked on paper at the machine, so nobody saw the limit go by

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: H22 hub bores - WC-BROACH-01 - parts broached after the tool passed 30,000 strokes on 2026-06-21
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: H18 hubs on WC-BROACH-02 - same part family, tool replaced on schedule
isIsNot.notes: Defect starts at the stroke count overrun, not at a batch or shift change

customerReference.complaintReference: N/A - internal defect, no customer reference
